name: Close the month and produce the fund's net asset value (one monthly close)
summary: Each month fund accounting closes the investment ledger and produces the fund's month-end net asset value for the base and additional plan accounts, which performance measurement uses for monthly returns and, each quarter, the financial statements team uses for the statements due to the ministers within 45 days. Accountants confirm the month's daily cycles are closed, reconcile every sub-ledger to the ledger and to custodian and counterparty statements, book fee, interest and expense accruals, record external managers' month-end values or estimates, and either roll private values forward for cash flows or, in quarter-end months, record the newly approved private valuations. Senior associates review reconciliations and journals, the director approves the NAV pack and the controller gives final approval. Late manager values and the wait for quarter-end private valuations set the length of the close.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund investment manager that invests one fund globally with mostly internal teams, keeps its books in SimCorp Dimension and a corporate ERP, and reports as an IFRS investment entity.
baseline.notes: One case per month; one month in three is a quarter-end close that waits for approved private valuations and feeds the quarterly financial statements.

trigger: The last business day of the month ends and the month-end batch runs on the final daily ledger.
end_state: The controller approves the month-end net asset value, the period is locked and the NAV is sent to performance measurement and, at quarter end, to financial statements.

volume.seasonality: Quarter-end months (June, September, December, March) take several weeks longer because of private valuations; the March close also feeds the annual report due within 60 days.

evidence.note: Monthly valuation required for total fund returns under GIPS; quarterly statements and annual report deadlines under the fund's governing act.

Close tasks match the model fund investment accounting posting. Title and loaded cost from the organisation file. systems.name: SimCorp Dimension investment book of record (portfolio accounting, treasury, performance)
Corporate ERP (general ledger, accounts payable, budgeting)
Private investments administration and cash flow system
General partner and fund administrator investor portals
Global custodian web portal and statements

steps.name: Run the month-end batch
steps.description: On the last business day SimCorp takes the month-end prices and FX rates from the daily valuation, runs month-end accruals and amortisation and produces the preliminary month-end balances once the last daily ledger is closed.

error.defect_description: A late price or rate is captured.

evidence.note: Month-end valuation as of the last business day (GIPS) and period-end close in SimCorp (posting). Timing is the author's estimate; month ends on weekends add up to two days.

steps.name: Confirm the close calendar and cut-offs with input owners
steps.description: A senior associate confirms the close calendar with operations, valuations, expense management, payroll and the external managers team: the dates by which late trades, accruals, manager NAVs and private valuations must reach fund accounting.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Close calendar with checkpoints for cut-offs.

steps.name: Confirm the month's daily cycles are closed and apply cut-off
steps.description: An accountant checks that every daily ledger in the month was signed off, that trades booked late with month-end trade dates are in, and that suspense is cleared or listed with an owner.

error.defect_description: A late trade is missed.

evidence.note: Pre-close readiness and suspense clearing before close.

steps.name: Prepare month-end reconciliations
steps.description: Accountants reconcile every sub-ledger to the general ledger and the custodian, bank and counterparty month-end statements for cash, positions, pending trades, receivables, payables, collateral and debt, and document each reconciling item with preparer evidence.

error.defect_description: A reconciling item is explained with weak evidence.

control.basis: Month-end account reconciliations with preparer and reviewer evidence as key controls over financial reporting (COSO 2013), certified by the CEO and CFRO and audited by the external auditor

evidence.note: Sub-ledger to general ledger reconciliations in the posting; ICFR certification and audit; manual reconciliations as the main close burden in the SimCorp case. Minutes are the author's estimate of team effort.

steps.name: Book month-end accruals and corporate ledger postings
steps.description: Accountants accrue external management and performance fees from manager reports and agreements, interest on term debt and commercial paper, and take in the month's operating expense and payroll postings from the corporate ledger, then allocate costs between the base and additional plan accounts.

error.defect_description: A performance fee accrual misses a change in terms or crystallisation date.

evidence.note: Fee accruals tied to terms and crystallisation; separate base and additional plan accounts.

steps.name: Run close status meetings and track the checklist
steps.description: The director holds short close calls through the first week and a half, tracks each checklist item and late input, and decides which items can be estimated and which must wait.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; readiness tracking appears in the FundCount workflow.

steps.name: Wait for external managers' month-end values
steps.description: External hedge fund and public market managers and fund administrators deliver month-end NAV statements or estimates through portals and email, typically one to two weeks after month end.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: some values missing at the cut-off

evidence.note: Fund investments valued at NAV reported by administrators or managers; estimated values allowed with later true-up. Arrival times and the 25% late share are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Chase late external fund values
steps.description: A senior associate chases managers and administrators that have not reported, with the external manager monitoring team, and agrees an estimate based on the manager's flash return or the prior value rolled forward where no value arrives in time.

error.defect_description: Estimate differs materially from the final value.

evidence.note: Use of preliminary estimated values with assessment of the difference later (GIPS 22.A.18).

steps.name: Record external fund values and true up prior estimates
steps.description: Accountants record the month-end external fund values, replace last month's estimates with final values and book the difference, and keep a log of estimates used so they can be trued up next month.

error.defect_description: Value recorded in the wrong currency or for the wrong share class.

evidence.note: Adjust when final values are received (GIPS 22.A.18); quarter-end share is one month in three.

steps.name: Hand over approved quarter-end private valuations
steps.description: In quarter-end months the valuations team sends the private investment fair values approved through its quarterly process and the Valuation Committee, with a schedule of each holding's value, change, method and roll-forward adjustments.

error.defect_description: Schedule omits a holding or a late change.

evidence.note: Finance valuation governance and quarterly valuation of private investments; the wait reflects GP reports arriving weeks after quarter end and is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Record private valuations and holding subsidiary fair values
steps.description: Accountants post the change in fair value of each private investment and update the fair value of each investment holding subsidiary from its underlying investments, debt and accumulated income, and reconcile the totals to the valuation schedule.

error.defect_description: A valuation is posted to the wrong holding or subsidiary.

evidence.note: Investment holding subsidiaries measured at fair value based on their underlying investments, liabilities and accumulated net income.

steps.name: Check recorded values against approved valuations
steps.description: A valuations senior compares the values recorded in the ledger with the approved valuation schedule and the data used for the fair value hierarchy disclosures, and signs that they agree or lists corrections.

error.defect_description: A mismatch is missed.

control.basis: Valuation policy and Valuation Committee governance: recorded fair values must agree with approved valuations, with Finance oversight independent of investment departments

evidence.note: Valuation governance in the annual report; valuation review sign-off in the NAV workflow.

steps.name: Roll forward private values for the month's cash flows
steps.description: In months without new quarterly valuations, accountants carry each private holding at its last approved value adjusted for capital calls, distributions and FX since the valuation date, and note any known event that may need a valuation update.

error.defect_description: A cash flow is missed in the roll-forward.

evidence.note: Last available value used as fair value between valuation dates (GIPS 22.A.18).

steps.name: Run the month-end NAV and account allocation
steps.description: SimCorp recalculates month-end net assets with all accruals, fund values and private values, allocates income and net assets between the base and additional plan accounts, and produces the trial balance and NAV pack.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Separate net assets and net income of the base and additional plan accounts.

steps.name: Analyse NAV movements and write variance commentary
steps.description: Accountants compare the month's change in net assets by asset class and department with returns, cash flows and plan transfers, explain large variances in commentary, and list unexplained items for review.

error.defect_description: An unusual movement is explained away.

evidence.note: Analytical review with variance commentary; unexplained NAV movement is a stop-the-line condition.

steps.name: Review reconciliations, accruals and journals
steps.description: Senior associates review and sign each reconciliation, the accrual calculations, the estimate log and every manual journal of the close with its support, and send corrections back to the preparers.

error.defect_description: A weak reconciling item is accepted.

control.basis: Preparer and reviewer sign-off on reconciliations and manual journals within internal control over financial reporting (COSO 2013)

evidence.note: Preparer and approver stamps; separation of preparation from approval; ICFR framework.

steps.name: Post adjusting journals and re-run
steps.description: Accountants book the corrections and late items with support and reason codes, and the NAV is recalculated for another review.

error.defect_description: Correction introduces a new error.

evidence.note: Adjusting journal entries in the posting; support and reason codes for manual journals.

steps.name: Review and approve the NAV pack
steps.description: The director reviews the NAV pack, variance commentary, open items, estimates used and stop-the-line conditions, challenges the team on large movements and approves the pack or sends items back.

error.defect_description: An open item is accepted without enough evidence.

control.basis: Close policy: director approval of the month-end NAV pack before release

evidence.note: Final NAV approval with documented approvers.

steps.name: Give final approval of the month-end NAV
steps.description: The managing director and controller reviews the summary NAV, the key judgments, estimates and open items, and approves the month-end net asset value, which supports the CEO and CFRO certification at year end.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: CEO/CFRO certification of internal control over financial reporting (COSO 2013) supported by controller sign-off of period results; external auditor's ICFR audit

evidence.note: CEO/CFRO ICFR certification and external audit of ICFR; controller sign-off as the support for it is the author's assumption.

steps.name: Lock the period and distribute the NAV
steps.description: An accountant locks the month in SimCorp and the corporate ledger, files the close evidence, and sends the approved net asset values to performance measurement and, in quarter-end months, to the financial statements team.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Monthly, quarterly and annual schedules and audit support in the posting.

exceptions.name: Quarter-end close with private valuations
exceptions.description: The close waits for the valuations team's approved quarter-end private values, which depend on GP and partner reports arriving weeks after quarter end; accountants then record values and subsidiary fair values and valuations checks them.

exceptions.name: Late external manager values
exceptions.description: Some managers or administrators miss the cut-off; the senior chases them and an estimate is used and trued up next month.

exceptions.name: Review corrections and re-run
exceptions.description: Senior, director or controller review finds errors or late items; adjusting journals are posted and the NAV is re-run and reviewed again.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the last business day of the month to controller approval of the month-end NAV
benchmarks.population: Monthly NAV close at a large asset owner with private assets, two ordinary months and one quarter-end month per quarter

evidence.note: No published figure for this organisation. Ordinary months are assumed to close in about two weeks because manager values arrive one to two weeks after month end (longer than the APQC corporate median of 6.4 days and the eight business days in the SimCorp pension case); quarter-end months must close in time for statements due within 45 days.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from trial balance to consolidated statements
benchmarks.population: About 2,300 organisations in APQC's General Accounting benchmark (all industries)

evidence.note: Top quartile 4.8 days or less, bottom quartile 10 days or more.

benchmarks.metric: month-end close at a large US public pension before automation
benchmarks.population: One US public pension fund over USD 100 billion with an eight-person investment accounting team

evidence.note: Vendor case study.

benchmarks.population: The model fund, first three fiscal quarters

evidence.note: the fund's governing act s. 50(1).

pain_points.description: External managers and administrators report month-end values one to two weeks late, so estimates are used and trued up the following month.

evidence.note: Preliminary values with later adjustment under GIPS 22.A.18.

pain_points.description: Quarter-end closes wait weeks for private valuations, which are themselves based on GP and partner reports that lag the quarter end.

evidence.note: Private valuations through Finance governance; GP reporting obligations such as annual information within 90 days.

pain_points.description: Month-end reconciliations across custodians, counterparties, sub-ledgers and holding subsidiaries take most of the team's time, with spreadsheets for evidence.

evidence.note: Manual reconciliations as the main close burden; sub-ledger to ledger reconciliations in the posting.

pain_points.description: Three review layers (senior, director, controller) each add a wait for availability, and corrections loop back through re-runs.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Quarterly financial statements to the ministers within 45 days after each of the first three quarters (s. 50(1)); annual report within 60 days after the financial year end (s. 51(1)); special examination at least every six years (s. 47(1)).

sources.title: 2020 GIPS Standards for Asset Owners
sources.supports: Total funds valued at least monthly as of month end and private market portfolios at least quarterly; when the last available historical price or a preliminary estimated value is used, assess the difference from the final value and adjust when it is received (22.A.18, 22.A.20, 22.A.30).

sources.title: Metric of the Month: Cycle Time for Monthly Close
sources.supports: APQC General Accounting benchmark, about 2,300 organisations: monthly close from trial balance to consolidated statements takes 4.8 calendar days or less for the top quartile, a median of 6.4 days and 10 or more days for the bottom quartile.

sources.title: Large US public pension achieves significant efficiency gains with SimCorp
sources.supports: A US public pension fund with over USD 100 billion: before its move to SimCorp Dimension the month-end close took the whole eight-person investment accounting team at least eight business days, with manual reconciliations between systems; afterwards one to two business days per accountant (vendor-reported).

sources.title: NAV Oversight: Controls, Review Workflow, and Common Breakpoints
sources.supports: Eight-step NAV review workflow: pre-close readiness, reconciliation review, valuation review, accruals review, allocations, analytical review with variance commentary, final NAV approval with documented approvers, post-close retrospective; stop-the-line conditions such as unreconciled cash or positions, missing valuation approvals and unexplained NAV movement; manual journals need support and reason codes.

sources.title: Month-End Close Errors: Controller's 20-Point Checklist
sources.supports: Close calendar with checkpoints; clear suspense so nothing ages beyond one close; preparer and approver stamps on material journals and reconciliations; close only after exceptions are cleared or tracked.

sources.supports: Limited partners should receive quarterly unaudited statements and a summary of capital calls and distributions, and annual information within 90 days of year end.

assumptions: One month in three is a quarter-end close; the simulated distribution mixes both, so its median reflects ordinary months and its 90th percentile the quarter-end months.

Touch minutes are team person-minutes per close; several accountants work reconciliations, accruals and fund values in parallel, so the simulator, which adds them in sequence, overstates elapsed time by a few days in an ordinary month.

fte_on_process (about 3.2 FTE) averages close work over the month; the organisation file gives 45 accountants and 25 seniors in fund accounting and financial reporting, who also run daily accounting, financial statements, holding subsidiary accounts and audit.
The wait for quarter-end private valuations (mode 12 days after manager values arrive) is the author's estimate chosen so quarter-end closes finish within the 45-day statement deadline.
The month-end close for this organisation is not published; the 14-day median and 35-day 90th percentile are the author's estimates.
Operating expense and payroll postings arrive from the corporate ERP (fin-expense-management and tal-payroll) and are allocated between the base and additional plan accounts in step s05.
Loaded hourly costs are the organisation file's, which include incentive pay and a 1.25 overhead factor; they are far above the Job Bank Toronto median for NOC 11100 of 41.34 an hour (2023-2024).

The simulated median cycle time (about 19 days) is above the 14-day benchmark estimate mainly because parallel close work is added in sequence by the simulator; the 90th percentile (about 34 days) matches quarter-end closes that finish inside the 45-day statement deadline.
